chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man and Sayf ibn Umayrah, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: A man has nothing of the fitrah except what would suffice to discharge it on behalf of himself alone. Should he give it to a stranger, or should he and his dependants eat it? He said: He should give it to some of his dependants, then the other should give it on behalf of himself; they should pass it around among themselves, so that one fitrah counts on behalf of all of them.

key_terms.الْفِطْرَةِ: Zakat al-Fitrah, the alms due at the end of Ramadan
key_terms.غَرِيبًا: a stranger, meaning someone outside his household
key_terms.فِطْرَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ: a single fitrah counted on behalf of all of them
key_terms.يُرَدِّدُونَهَا: they pass it around from one to another

ai.seo_question: What should a poor person do if he has only enough for one fitrah for himself and his family?
ai.summary: This hadith explains a legal ruling concerning Zakat al-Fitrah for a poor person who possesses only enough to pay one fitrah. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام instructs that it may be circulated among the members of his household so that a single fitrah serves on behalf of them all. The report reflects legal facilitation for the poor and the household-based handling of this obligation.
